title: Kingdom of Vaspurakan
capsule: Vaspurakan was a medieval Armenian kingdom centred on the shores of Lake Van, ruled by the Artsruni dynasty from its formal establishment in 908 under Khachik-Gagik I. The kingdom reached its apex under Gagik I (r. 908–943), who assumed the title 'King of Armenia' and commissioned the celebrated Church of the Holy Cross on Aghtamar island, one of the masterworks of Armenian medieval architecture. Persistent Seljuq raiding after 1016 weakened the state irrecoverably; in 1021 King Senekerim-Hovhannes voluntarily ceded the kingdom to the Byzantine emperor Basil II in exchange for the region of Sebasteia in Cappadocia, ending Armenian sovereignty over the Van basin.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Vaspurakan's core around Lake Van is well-attested through Armenian, Byzantine, and Arab sources; peripheral districts changed hands frequently, making exact boundaries uncertain.
